title: I've been building an isometric character creator. Just added Elves and rebuilt the Orcs.
author: TheSpriteWizard
selftext:
Hey everyone, Sprite Wizard here.

I've been working on SpriteForge, a character creator built on the rendering system I developed for SpritePress.

The idea is to make it easier to create consistent pixel-art characters across different animations and viewing angles. It's particularly useful if you're working with AI in your development process but want more control over how your characters actually look from frame to frame.

I just released updates 0.5.0 and 0.5.1, so I thought I'd share the progress.

**What's changed:**

* Added male and female Elves, bringing the total to four customizable species: Humans, Goblins, Orcs, and Elves.
* Rebuilt both Orc models so they can use the entire clothing and equipment library.
* Improved equipment fitting across different body types.
* Added a capture guide explaining how frame rates, animations, and directional rendering affect the final sprite sheet.
* Improved loading times and fixed a few clothing issues.

The tool currently has 71 animations, up to 16 rendering directions, and hundreds of interchangeable clothing and equipment pieces.

There's no generative AI in the actual rendering process. It uses 3D models and animations to produce consistent sprites. I've found this approach useful for avoiding some of the character consistency problems that come with generating individual frames.

**The browser version is free on** [**itch.io**](http://itch.io), so there's no need to purchase or download anything to use the character creator.

[https://thespritewizard.itch.io/sprite-forge-kanes-character-creator](https://thespritewizard.itch.io/sprite-forge-kanes-character-creator)

I'm still adding species and improving the equipment system. Dwarves, Zombies, and Ghosts are next on my list.

If anyone gives it a try, I'd be interested in hearing how well the sprites fit into your workflow, particularly if you're already using AI-generated assets in your projects.

I'm also interested in what other developers are doing to maintain character consistency across animations.

Thanks for taking a look.
